external_entities.notes: The source describes three partners but does not distinguish them by name.

external_entities.description: An analyst who queries the warehouse directly.
external_entities.notes: The source refers to analysts collectively.

processes.name: Airflow scheduler
processes.description: A scheduler that wakes at 02:00, lists the landing bucket, reads files, and triggers a Spark transform job.
processes.source_excerpt: An Airflow scheduler running in the landing network wakes up at 02:00, lists the bucket, and reads whatever is there.
processes.notes: It does not check that a file came from the partner whose folder it landed in.

processes.name: Spark transform job
processes.description: A transform job that normalizes records and loads them into BigQuery.
processes.source_excerpt: For each file the scheduler triggers a Spark transform job in the warehouse network.
processes.notes: Nothing validates the row contents beyond the schema.

data_stores.name: landing bucket
data_stores.description: A bucket into which insurance partners push daily extract files.
data_stores.source_excerpt: They push files into a landing bucket over SFTP.
data_stores.notes: I don't know how the landing bucket is encrypted or whether the Airflow metadata database is encrypted at rest. Both are on defaults as far as I know.

data_stores.name: Airflow metadata database
data_stores.description: Airflow's metadata database, which stores connection strings and partner keys.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Airflow keeps its connection strings and the partner keys in its own metadata database.
data_stores.notes: I don't know how the landing bucket is encrypted or whether the Airflow metadata database is encrypted at rest. Both are on defaults as far as I know.

data_stores.name: BigQuery
data_stores.description: The warehouse into which the Spark transform job loads normalized claim records and which analysts query directly.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The transform normalizes the records and loads them into BigQuery.
data_stores.notes: The analyst grant is dataset-wide, and member-identifying columns have not been split out.

data_flows.data_description: Claim-record extract files with member names and dates of birth.

data_flows.notes: Nothing validates the row contents beyond the schema.

assumptions.assumption: The insurance partner is an external system rather than a human actor because it pushes files into the pipeline.
assumptions.basis: The source says the partners push files into the landing bucket.

assumptions.assumption: The analyst is a human actor because the source describes analysts querying the warehouse.
assumptions.basis: The source explicitly identifies the actors as analysts.

assumptions.assumption: The Airflow scheduler presents a non-web interface because it is described as a scheduler running a batch pipeline.
assumptions.basis: The source describes an Airflow scheduler that wakes nightly, lists a bucket, reads files, and triggers a job.

assumptions.assumption: The Spark transform job presents a non-web interface because it is described as a transform job processing files.
assumptions.basis: The source describes a Spark transform job that normalizes records and loads them into BigQuery.

assumptions.assumption: The landing bucket contains confidential data because its extracts contain member names, dates of birth, and claim records.
assumptions.basis: The source says the extracts contain claim records with member names and dates of birth.

assumptions.assumption: The Airflow metadata database contains confidential data because it stores connection strings and partner keys.
assumptions.basis: The source says Airflow keeps connection strings and partner keys in the database.

assumptions.assumption: BigQuery contains confidential data because it stores claim records with member-identifying information.
assumptions.basis: The source says the transform loads claim records into BigQuery and that member-identifying columns have not been split out.
